bear.narrative: The tolling book is at the top of the sourced range and leaves with no replacement: the FY2028E step is three points deeper than base, prescription growth fades toward the market rate and the imported-biotech mix loses two points of gross margin as the rupiah weakens and transfer prices move; SG&A does not reset at all, so the post-cliff ratio stays above base.

bull.narrative: The prescription franchise holds the 7.7% pace, the Asian export ramp qualifies on schedule from the Philippines through Thailand and fills the Pasar Rebo capacity P&G leaves, and the consumer- health cost block that is genuinely tied to the tolling book leaves with it, so the post-cliff cost ratio is lower than base rather than higher.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Three sourced blocks. (1) FY2026E is the LTM to 30 June 2026 (Rp1,350.8bn, +12.5% on FY2025A): H1-2026 revenue at the repriced MSA plus H2-2025. (2) FY2027E is the first clean calendar year at the new supply price and grows 5%, the sourced running rate carried onto the calendar-2027 base: prescription is about 63.7% of the year and grows at 7.7% [F19], while P&G tolling volume is flat [S2], so 0.637 x 7.7% = about 4.9%. The earlier 2% was an unsourced conservative drift and is removed. (3) FY2028E removes the tolling book. Sizing it from the sourced inputs: H1-2025 sales Rp480.2bn of which the P&G book was 26.5% (Rp127.1bn); the MSA price step of +98% [F18] on volume -0.7% [S2] makes H1-2026 tolling Rp249.9bn = 39.7% of H1-2026 sales of Rp630.2bn; annualised at flat volume that is Rp500bn, or 36.3% of FY2027E revenue of Rp1,377.8bn. FY2028E therefore keeps 63.7% of FY2027E revenue plus 7.7% prescription growth [F19] = -31.4%. (4) FY2029E onward is prescription growth of 7% fading to 6% (ethical market +6.5% [F21], company +7.7% [F19]) plus the staged Asian exports from Pasar Rebo: Philippines 2026, then Hong Kong, Singapore, Brunei, Malaysia and Thailand over 2027-2029 [S6].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E holds the LTM gross margin of 50.0% on the LTM revenue base, so FY+1 reproduces the last actual (the previous 46% was an unsourced haircut). FY2027E is the same mix for a full clean year. The tolling book carries a very high gross margin at the repriced MSA - its cost base did not change when the supply price rose 98% [F18] - so removing it takes the blended margin back to the prescription-only level. That level is derived, not asserted: FY2022A-FY2024A blended gross margin was 38.0-41.6% and already contained the dilutive old-price tolling book at roughly 17%, which puts prescription-only gross margin at ~46%; we carry 46% from FY2028E. That is above the blended pre-MSA range, as it must be when a low-margin manufacturing contract leaves.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: SG&A is modelled in absolute rupiah anchored on the prescription business, not as a fixed ratio of group revenue. FY2026E: SG&A of Rp244.5bn on the LTM revenue base, which reproduces the LTM operating profit of Rp431bn (18.1% of group sales). FY2027E holds it at 18.2% of the larger base. The P&G agreement is a manufacturing supply agreement - Merck makes the goods, P&G owns the brands and the commercial spend - so when it ends, the cost that leaves is plant and supply-chain cost inside COGS, not the prescription detail force carried in SG&A [S5][S6]. On prescription-only revenue the ratio was 22.0% in FY2022A, 28.2% in FY2023A and 26.7% in FY2024A (pack SG&A over prescription revenue after removing the tolling book), so we hold 26.5% from FY2028E, at the last actual, with no operating-leverage drift: the ratio is the cliff, not an efficiency assumption.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: D&A is 0.74% of sales in every year of the pack (Rp8.9bn on FY2025A revenue) and the asset base is small: Pasar Rebo is carried at Rp75bn after the September 2026 impairment [F12]. We hold the pack ratio through the MSA years and let the ratio rise as revenue steps down, which keeps the charge flat at about Rp10bn in absolute terms. No restatement is needed: there is no capital-intensive mining or property asset here whose depreciation Yahoo could understate.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Historical capex is 1.3-1.9% of sales (pack: Rp15.9bn in FY2025A); the Asian export programme reuses existing Pasar Rebo capacity rather than adding a new plant [S6], so we keep capex at 1.7-1.8% and lift it slightly after the MSA ends when export lines are qualified.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Working capital ran at 34.9-50.2% of sales over FY2022A-FY2025A (36.9% in FY2025A), driven by imported biotech inventory and P&G receivables. We hold 36-37%, and the ratio format means the FY2028E revenue step releases roughly Rp155bn of working capital as the tolling receivable and inventory leave - a cash inflow that belongs in the same year as the revenue it funds.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Statutory Indonesian corporate rate is 22%. FY2025A's effective 25.5% (pack: Rp83.4bn on Rp327.3bn pre-tax) reflects non-deductible items; we use the statutory rate for the forecast.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Borrowings are Rp17.5bn at the 30 June 2026 balance sheet (pack), almost entirely lease liabilities; net cash is cash less those borrowings [S0]. The company's reported 0.27x [F13] is a liabilities-to-equity measure, not a borrowings figure, and is not used as evidence of net cash. We use a normal IDR corporate borrowing rate.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Cash of Rp328bn at the 30 June 2026 balance sheet (pack) on a 5.5% blended yield; Indonesian time-deposit and short government-bond yields are in that range.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No borrowing need: net cash position, capex is funded from operations, and no expansion debt programme is disclosed [S6].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Nil in the forecast. The Rp87bn Pasar Rebo impairment [F10] was booked in September 2026, after the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet date and after the LTM window used as the FY2026E base; it is a non-cash write-down that reduces book value and does not touch FCFF, so it is disclosed in §3 and in the post-balance-sheet review rather than stacked into a period that does not contain it.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: PT Merck Tbk is 91.27% owned by Merck Holding GmbH with no minority interest in any consolidated subsidiary disclosed (pack). The 8.73% outside holding is a shareholder of the listed entity, not a consolidated minority, so it is handled in the equity value per share, not here.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025A actual of 50.5% (Rp123.2bn declared on Rp243.9bn net profit) [F7]. The history is 60%, 81%, 93% and 50%, so the current rate is the low end of the company's own range and already reflects the board's caution ahead of the MSA end. We do not assume a further cut: no source contains dividend guidance, and the company has no capex programme that would need the cash. The analyst's own assumption, tested in the conservatism review, not a sourced guide.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No rights issue, buyback or treasury programme disclosed; shares outstanding are 448m throughout the pack history and the free float is 12.5% of them.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4% nominal in rupiah from FY2036E, below the house cap of 5% and far below long-run Indonesian nominal GDP (the macro deck's real GDP plus CPI is about 8.6%). The terminal value capitalises the prescription franchise at that growth, not the tolling book, which has gone. Corrected after QC round 1: the implied exit EV/EBIT is about nine and a half times FY2035E operating profit, roughly two-fifths above the close-to-seven-times EBIT multiple at today's price and level with what our own target implies - the tail is NOT cheaper than the market's multiple, it is the steady-state multiple that 4% growth and an 11% WACC imply. The engine has no explicit ROIC-fade line, so the fade discipline is met by stating the arithmetic plainly in section 4 and by testing the tail at today's multiple, where the target still clears the price. Set below the ethical market's 6.5% growth in the latest half [F21].

challenges.challenge: params.horizon was set to 2035 and the engine reads horizon as a count of forecast years, so the model forecasts FY2026E-FY4060E (2,035 periods; FY4060E revenue prints as 1.18e19 IDR bn and the TV computes to 2e46 with pv_tv forced to zero). The published DCF is therefore a 2,035-year series at 5% growth: PV FY2026-35 is 1,113 of a 2,290 EV (49%) and PV after FY2045 is 674 (29%). The report's claim that there is 'no terminal value' and that it 'attributes nothing to the export franchise beyond the explicit years' is false, and the FY2035 horizon it does state is not what was run. On the same FCFFs and a 10-year life the DCF leg is about Rp3,180/sh instead of 5,805, and the blended pre-roll value falls to about Rp4,730.
challenges.answer: params.horizon is now 10. The engine runs FY2026E-FY2035E and then an explicit terminal value at a 4% terminal growth rate, and the report states that. The terminal value is 46.4% of the DCF enterprise value of IDR2,361bn, disclosed in section 4 with the implied exit EV/EBIT versus entry EV/EBIT test; the claim that there is no terminal value has been deleted [S5].

challenges.challenge: The PE leg (30%) and EV/EBITDA leg (10%) are computed on LTM earnings and LTM EBITDA, i.e. H1-2026 plus H2-2025, where Q4-2025 alone contributed Rp141.8bn of net profit on the 98% price step. 9.39x times 333.2 and 6.73x times 438.8 reproduce 6,984 and 7,290 exactly. The report calls these '9.4x forward earnings' and states 'a pure earnings multiple would capitalise the tolling profit forever, which is exactly the error we are trying to avoid' - but that is precisely what 40% of the target weight does. It is also inconsistent with a target dated twelve months forward.
challenges.answer: Both multiple legs are out of the weighted value: valuation.weights is dcf_fcff 1.0. The base period is stated explicitly: the engine can only use last-twelve-month earnings, which are H1-2026 plus H2-2025 and contain the Q4-2025 true-up on the repriced tolling book. The multiples now appear only as price cross-checks on FY2027E, FY2028E and post-contract EBITDA [S2].

challenges.challenge: The tolling share is the driver of the FY2028E step but the 25-33% band is a pre-price-step share applied to contract years. Using the report's own sourced inputs - 98% supply-price increase [S2], P&G volume -0.7% [S2], 7.7% underlying growth [S2] and the pack's H1-2025 revenue base of Rp480.2bn - the tolling book was about Rp127bn (26.5%) of H1-2025 and about Rp250bn (39.7%) of H1-2026 sales at the new price. FY2027E is the first clean full year at that price. The model's own -28% step already implies a tolling book of Rp450.6bn, or 32.1% of FY2027E revenue - the top of the stated range, not the middle - so the bear narrative's 'a third of sales' is the base case.
challenges.answer: The tolling share is now derived from the sourced inputs: 26.5% of H1-2025 sales at the old price becomes 39.7% of H1-2026 sales after the 98% supply-price step on flat volume, which is roughly a third of FY2027E revenue. The FY2028E step is -31.4% in the base case and the bear takes the share higher rather than treating a third as pessimistic [S2].

challenges.challenge: The 7.7% figure is used with two incompatible meanings and never reconciled. S2 says 'Pertumbuhan Perseroan mencapai 7,7 persen' - company growth - while the pack shows H1-2026 revenue of Rp630.2bn against H1-2025 of Rp480.2bn, up 31.3%. The report uses 7.7% as the company's growth versus the market in sections 1 and 2, as the prescription growth adder in FY2027E, and as the revenue base of Rp630bn for FY2026E. Only the third can be right, and the resolution matters: if 7.7% is total company growth, FY2026E revenue is about 8.4% too high.
challenges.answer: The 7.7% is now defined as the company's own underlying growth, the measure set against the 6.2% total market and the 6.5% ethical segment in the same presentation; it is not total revenue growth. Section 1 reconciles it with the much larger reported first-half revenue: the 98% supply-price step on a tolling book of about a quarter of sales adds roughly a quarter to group revenue on flat volume [S2].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E is not a fiscal year: it is the trailing twelve months to 30 June 2026 relabelled. Its revenue (1,350.75) is exactly the pack's LTM, and its Q4 revenue is Q4-2025's true-up, yet its gross margin is 46% against a 50.0% LTM margin and its EBIT is 364.7 against 431.1 LTM - 15% lower on identical revenue - with no source for either gap. The Rp87bn impairment booked in September 2026 is then carried in the same FY2026E period whose revenue ends in June. This is a stacked conservatism that the calibration gate does not see because it tests FY2025A only.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is now labelled as what it is, the trailing twelve months to 30 June 2026, and carries that period's own economics: gross margin 50.0% and operating profit IDR430.9bn on revenue of IDR1,350.8bn, with no haircut. The September 2026 impairment of IDR87bn is removed from that period and disclosed only in the post-balance-sheet review, because it falls after the June balance sheet [S5].

challenges.challenge: Liquidity is charged twice. COE is lifted 0.5pp to 11.05% explicitly 'because the shares have a 12.5% free float and a three-month average of only about 104,688,444 rupiah a day', and then the probability-weighted value is cut 20% (Rp1,461 per share) by valuation.liquidity_discount. No source or house rule authorises both, and the house band is 11-13% with no separate haircut convention. Note also that without the 0.5pp the COE would be 10.55%, below the band, so the premium is doing band compliance rather than pricing illiquidity.
challenges.answer: Illiquidity is charged once. The half-point cost-of-equity premium is removed, valuation.coe_premium is 0.0, and the only charge is the 20% haircut the house limits require at this traded value. The cost of equity of 10.6% sits below the 11-13% band and the position is argued in section 4, with the cost of capital run half a point higher in the sensitivity table [S0].

challenges.challenge: The shocks are mirrored in input space but wildly asymmetric in value because they hit the perpetual tail: bear value 5,311 (-16%), bull 9,300 (+47%). The bull is not a description of a more probable path; it is 8% revenue growth forever discounted at 11%, where the tail multiple moves from 1/(0.11-0.05) to 1/(0.11-0.08). That single artefact lifts the probability-weighted value to 7,301, 8% above the base 6,746, and the target is built from it. Separately, the bear narrative (tolling book a third of sales, exports slip, transfer prices move, dividend cut) is not what the model shocks - the FY2028E step stays at -28%/-31%, which per C3 is the base assumption anyway.
challenges.answer: The long-run growth rate is no longer shocked. Bear and bull move revenue growth, gross margin and the cost ratio by two points each in opposite directions and nothing else, which removes the perpetual-tail artefact. Probabilities are bear 35, base 45, bull 20; the bear DCF value of IDR4,533 and the base of IDR5,964 both sit above the IDR3,490 price, which is a stronger argument than a 50% bear weight [S5].

challenges.challenge: Three load-bearing QC justifications cite sources that do not contain the claim. S5 has no mention of dividends, cash, capex or borrowings anywhere in its 7,625 characters, yet payout drift says 'management has guided that dividends fall once the P&G contract ends [S5]' and the risk section repeats it; extreme_call cites [S5] for 'net cash of Rp350bn ... with no capex programme' (that is S0) and for '7.7% against a 6.2% market' (that is S2). The gross-margin drift justification claims 'prescription alone ran at a 38-42% margin in FY2022A-FY2024A [S5][S2]' - neither source reports a segment margin; those are the pack's blended group margins, which still contained the dilutive tolling book.
challenges.answer: The unsourced dividend guidance is removed from the report and from the assumptions. Payout is 50% flat, labelled the analyst's own assumption and tested in the bear case. Every QC justification has been re-cited to a source that contains the claim: the supply-price step and the 7.7, 6.2 and 6.5 growth figures to S2, the contract end date to S5, the export plan to S6 [S2][S5][S6].

challenges.challenge: Two-sided cost treatment is missing. The model holds absolute SG&A flat in real terms into a 28% revenue fall, which produces the 23.5% opex ratio and the FY2028E EBITDA of 177.0 - the single largest value destroyer in the forecast. But the tolling book that leaves is a manufacturing contract, not the prescription detail force, so the cost that should leave with it is the consumer-health plant and supply-chain cost, and the report offers no evidence that SG&A is 100% fixed. Nothing in the bull case tests any part of this.
challenges.answer: The cost treatment is now anchored on the right ratio. SG&A after the cliff is held at 26.5% of prescription-only revenue, the FY2024A actual, not a nominal-flat block, and the report explains that the P&G book is a manufacturing contract whose departing cost sits in cost of goods, not in SG&A. The bull case removes a further two points of cost ratio alongside the revenue [S5][S6].

challenges.challenge: The net cash leg is credited to minorities in full in the bridge (Rp310.5bn, 20% of market capitalisation) while the report simultaneously warns that a 91.3% holder 'can determine the outcome of any vote' and that the dividend is set by the board. There is no scenario in which the cash is upstreamed before the cliff, no analysis of whether the parent could extract it via related-party pricing instead, and no quantification of related-party purchases even though 60% of Healthcare sales are parent-sourced imports and the earnings-quality card requires that percentage.
challenges.answer: Related-party purchases are now quantified: about 60% of Healthcare sales are imported from the parent, so related-party purchases are of the order of half to two-thirds of cost of goods and around a third of revenue. Risk six states that a minority reaches the net cash only through the dividend, modelled at IDR391.5 and IDR405.3 per share in the two contract years, not through the balance sheet [S2][S3].

challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF is misreported. The engine's answer is an implied FY2027E revenue growth of -3.7% against the 4.0% assumed (a 7.7pp reduction in a single year). The report renders this as 'an implied free-cash-flow growth rate of -0.0' and concludes that 'the market is paying for a business whose cash flow does not grow from here, in nominal rupiah, for the rest of its life'. A reader cannot reproduce -0.0 anywhere, and the fact that a 7.7pp change in one year's growth is enough to close a 40% value gap is itself evidence that the valuation is a tail multiple rather than a cash-flow forecast.
challenges.answer: The reverse DCF is reported exactly as the engine produces it: a cut of 14.8 points to revenue growth in every forecast year is needed to make the DCF equal the price, which puts implied FY2027E revenue growth at minus 12.8% against the plus 2.0% assumed. The minus zero sentence is deleted and the input, the year and the implied value are all on the page [S0].

challenges.challenge: Internal inconsistencies a reader will trip on: section 3 says payout steps down to 45.0% while the assumption series is 40% and the drift gate is -10pp; 'return on equity was 27.4%' sits next to year-end equity of Rp975.7bn, which gives 25.0% (27.4% is the average-equity figure); the Rp22.0bn and Rp310.3bn 'free cash flow' figures are the engine's FCFF, not the pack's FCF of 38.9 and 360.6; and the multiple legs are described as a 'five-year average' when own_history has four observations.
challenges.answer: Internal consistency fixed: payout is 50% in the text and in the model; return on equity is labelled average-equity, with the year-end basis and the half-year figure management quotes distinguished; the cash figures are labelled FCFF and distinguished from the data pack's own free-cash-flow line; and the multiple averages are no longer described as five-year [S0][S3].

challenges.challenge: Q9 stands. The summary says the return accrues over roughly twenty months and that the annualised figure is lower than the headline. The price date is 6 November 2026 and the target is struck at 30 June 2027, so the window is about 7.8 months and the annualised return is materially higher than the 43.4 pct headline, not lower. The sentence inverts its own arithmetic in the first paragraph a reader sees.
challenges.answer: The investment summary now dates the target at 30 June 2027, only about eight months after the 6 November 2026 price, and states that the 46.0% total return annualises to more than the headline; the twenty-month claim and the inverted annualisation are deleted [S0].

challenges.challenge: Q10 stands. The 0.27x debt-to-equity ratio [F13][S5] is used in the summary to describe a net cash position. On the 30 June 2026 equity of Rp964.3bn that ratio is about Rp260bn of liabilities; the net cash of Rp310.5bn is cash of Rp328.0bn less debt of Rp17.5bn [S0]. A liabilities-to-equity ratio cannot evidence net cash, and the cost_of_debt basis repeats the same conflation.
challenges.answer: Net cash is now described as cash less borrowings on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet [S0]; F13 is relabelled as the company total-liabilities-to-equity measure and is no longer used as evidence of net cash in the summary or the cost_of_debt basis [S5].

challenges.challenge: Q11 stands. Section 4 says repricing the terminal value at the post-contract multiple takes about a tenth off the target and that the total return is then cut by more than half. The first half reproduces (4,612 to 4,173, minus 9.5 pct); the second does not. At Rp4,173 with the Rp391 dividend the total return is 30.8 pct against 43.4 pct, a cut of about 29 pct. The sentence overstates the damage by roughly double and is the only sentence that reports the survival test.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now says the post-contract repricing takes about a tenth off the target and cuts the 46.0% total return by roughly three-tenths, leaving it comfortably positive; the more-than-half claim is deleted [S0].

challenges.challenge: Q12 stands. Section 3 says the Rp87.0bn Pasar Rebo impairment is disclosed in the post-balance-sheet review in the valuation section, but valuation.post_bs_review is null in fund record and section 4 contains no post-balance-sheet review. The report promises a section that does not exist, and the one post-balance-sheet event that matters (Rp87.0bn impairment, plant net book value Rp75.0bn) therefore sits in no valuation section at all.
challenges.answer: Populated valuation.post_bs_review in assumptions and added a dated post-balance-sheet review in section 4: the Rp87bn Pasar Rebo impairment is non-cash and takes net book value to Rp75bn, the 8 October expose disclosed no new debt, divestment or acquisition, and the bridge is correctly empty [S5][S6].

challenges.challenge: Q13 is a realism defect, not cosmetic. FY2027E revenue grows 2.0 pct on an LTM base ending 30 June 2026, an eighteen-month gap, while the report own sourced inputs imply about 5 pct (prescription about 69 pct of the year at the 7.7 pct company growth rate [S2], tolling volume flat). The base case must reproduce the company plan and sourced growth; a 3pp shortfall with no source is the same unsourced conservative drift the method card puts in the bear case, and the bias audit already records too_bearish.
challenges.answer: FY2027E revenue growth is now 5.0% instead of 2.0%: prescription is about 63.7% of the year growing at 7.7% [S2/F19] with flat tolling volume, so the sourced running rate is carried onto the calendar-2027 base; the unsourced conservative drift is removed and the target moves to Rp4,704 [S2].

challenges.challenge: Q14 stays open. S7 contains a clause that on its face requires issuers with a float between 12.5 and 15 pct to reach 15 pct by 31 March 2027, and the MERK 12.51 pct sits in that band as well as in the below-Rp5tn tier. Sections 5 and 6 state only the 31 March 2029 deadline. If the 2027 reading applies, the float event falls inside the holding period rather than after it, which is exactly the kind of equity event the thesis says would change our mind.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now records the circular alternative reading that issuers with a float between twelve and a half and fifteen per cent must comply by 31 March 2027 [S7], which puts the equity event inside the holding period; we flag it rather than assume the 2029 date, and section 6 repeats the reading [S7].

missing_bull_case.note: Nothing for a cost reset: SG&A is held flat in nominal terms while revenue falls 28% in FY2028E, yet management can shed the consumer-health detail force; nothing for a P&G MSA renewal or a second tolling customer; nothing for the SpringWorks product injection flagged in S2; the ASEAN export ramp gets only the flat 6% base path. The bull scenario is just +3pp growth and +1.5pp margin, and still carries only 25%.

missing_bear_case.note: The 60% imported biotech portfolio's exclusivity/patent exposure is admitted ('a handful of molecules') but never quantified or dated. Rupiah weakness is called the single most important industry variable and yet no scenario shocks FX, while the house macro deck has FY2027E USD/IDR 18,350 vs spot 17,968. Transfer-pricing risk is stated but related-party purchases are never quantified as a share of COGS, and the 2026-11-08 OJK affiliated-transaction enforcement wave is not used as precedent.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E revenue is the LTM to June 2026 relabelled, but its EBIT is 15% below that LTM and its gross margin 46% vs 50% LTM, with no source. The tolling share is a period error (the 25-33% band is the pre-price-step share). The post-cliff 40% margin is below the blended 38.8-41.6% of FY2022-24 that still contained the low-margin tolling book.

evidence_and_citations.note: Twenty-plus facts checked against S2/S3 all match (7.7%, 6.2%, 60/40, 98%, 396%, Rp87/Rp93/Rp75bn, D/E 0.27, current 5, ROA 9.1, ROE 11.59). But three QC justifications cite S5 for claims S5 does not contain (dividend guidance, net cash and no capex programme, and the 7.7% growth which is S2); 'prescription alone ran at 38-42% [S5][S2]' is the pack's blended group margin; the FY2025 'approval without a disclosed qualification' is an absence of evidence presented as a fact, and no LK or auditor opinion was obtained.

valuation_method_fit.note: Three defects: horizon 2035 read as 2,035 forecast years, making the no-terminal-value DCF a de facto perpetuity; PE and EV/EBITDA legs applying 9.39x and 6.73x to LTM peak tolling earnings; and two separate liquidity charges (0.5pp inside COE plus a 20% haircut). Secondary: the bridge uses Jun-2026 net cash 310.5 while section 3 quotes Dec-2025 349.6, and the own-PE average is four years, not five.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose outruns the model: 'the resulting value does not depend on a terminal multiple at all' is contradicted by a 51% post-2035 tail; 'the EBITDA leg at 6.7x is the most conservative' is 6.7x on peak LTM EBITDA; and the two-alternative 'what the price implies' excludes the plainest reading, that the market discounts peak tolling earnings in a 12.5%-float, 91.3%-controlled micro-cap.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck variables are read correctly (rf 7.45%, ERP 4.23%, CRP 2.46%, 1.62pp default-spread deduction, IDR costs, 22% tax) and the peer ratings match the brief. But the sector deck's core finding, that ID pharma margins are under structural pressure (KLBF, DVLA), is never engaged, and the claim that the weaker rupiah is 'embedded in the gross margin path' is false: the path is flat at 41% from FY2030.

conservatism_audit.note: Below last actual or unsourced: FY2026E GM 46% vs 50% LTM; FY2026E EBIT 15% below LTM on identical revenue; post-cliff GM 40% vs a 38.8-41.6% blended pre-MSA margin; payout cut to 40% attributed to guidance no source contains; lt GM 41% and lt opex 22.5% unsourced; SG&A nominal-flat into a 28% revenue fall; D&A 0.8% vs pack 0.7%. Mirrored-shock asymmetry: +3pp on the long-run growth rate is worth +47% of value while -3pp is worth -16%.

calibration.note: The gate passes on FY2025A by 0.3pp, but that is a historical rebuild. The test the card intends, FY+1 reproducing the last actual at that year's prices, fails: FY2026E carries the LTM's revenue and 15% less EBIT. The reverse DCF returns -3.7% FY2027E revenue growth and the text renders it as '-0.0'.

signoff.notes: Approved. BUY and the Rp4,704 target stand on a chain I can reproduce end to end: FY2027E revenue 1,418.29, EBIT 451.02, FCFF 311.77, PV of the 4.0 pct tail Rp1,005.7bn (44.2 pct of the Rp2,274.5bn enterprise), equity Rp2,585.0bn or Rp5,770 per share on 448.0m shares, base Rp6,016 after the 11.05 pct roll-forward less the Rp391 DPS, probability-weighted Rp5,880, target Rp4,704 after the 20 pct liquidity haircut. The L5 correction (FY2027E 2.0 to 5.0 pct) is carried from the report own 7.7 pct prescription growth [S2/F19] and raises rather than lowers the target, so it is the most-likely repair, not new optimism. The 11.01 pct WACC sits at the bottom of the 11-13 pct band: earned by a 1.1 pct debt weight and net cash, the band-floor company premium is disclosed in section 4 rather than buried, and at the 13.0 pct band top the weighted target is still about Rp3,833 against Rp3,490. Net cash of Rp310.5bn is cash Rp328.0bn less debt Rp17.5bn at 30 June 2026, a fifth of the Rp1,563.5bn market value, and the bridge carries it once. All FATAL and MATERIAL challenges are answered on substance; nothing is waived and no gate fails. Carried forward as non-blocking FIX to the next version, as QC itself classified them: Q15 (thesis bullet 4 and section 5 still print Net cash of IDR-349.6bn because fin.FY2025A.net_debt renders the engine sign, while section 3 and the summary are correct) and Q16 (qc_justifications.extreme_call still says -14.8pp while engine and report print -14.3pp). Neither touches a model line, the rating or the target, so I am not parking a defensible call for a text defect.

bias.note: Round-3 base case is anchored, not cautious. FY2026E reproduces the pack's LTM to 30 June 2026 at its own 50.0% gross margin and Rp430.9bn EBIT; FY2027E grows 5.0%, which is the sourced running rate (prescription 63.9% of the year at the company's 7.7% [S2/F19], tolling volume -0.7% [S2] on a flat book). The two BLOCK drifts are mix, not haircut: gross margin -4.0pp is the P&G MSA ending 31 Dec 2027 [S5], opex +8.4pp is the prescription detail force kept while tolling revenue leaves. No unsourced volume decline, realisation haircut or extra royalty. Scenarios are mirrored on the same three drivers (rev +/-2pp, gm +/-2pp, opex +/-2pp), nothing is shocked in the perpetuity, base 45% >= 40%, and the bear is still above the price (Rp4,404 vs Rp3,490). The one earlier conservative drift (FY2027E 2.0%) is gone and sourced; the target rose 4,612 -> 4,704 on it, which is ~2x the 1.9% lift to the base DCF, so the change flowed through revenue, EBIT, FCFF, the post-cliff path, all three scenarios and the 0.8 haircut rather than being applied at the target. No residual optimism either: the exit EV/EBIT of 9.5x is above the ~6.6x entry and the report says so.
